routes.description: Establish that the universe, life, rationality, morality, and human experience are jointly more intelligible as products of a personal creator than of unguided natural processes alone.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its positive indicators support creative intelligence, naturalistic alternatives do not exhaust their explanatory force, and further evidence connects that intelligence to Christian theism.

motionBridge.description: Show that the cumulative evidence points beyond atheistic naturalism toward a personal creator and, with additional evidence, toward Christian theism.

centralBridges.description: Explain why rational and mathematical intelligibility is expected if a rational mind grounds the universe.
Show why the origin and semiotic character of biological information require explanation beyond evolutionary transmission and selection.
Ground objective moral significance and personal accountability in a reality deeper than unguided physical processes.
Connect general creator evidence to specifically Christian claims through historical, biblical, experiential, and personal evidence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish explanations by natural mechanism from explanations by personal agency so that the two are not treated as mutually exclusive.
Account for life-permitting cosmic conditions as evidence relevant to whether the universe has an intelligent source.

routes.description: Establish that scientific mechanisms, emergent order, evolved capacities, and evidence-based inquiry can account for the disputed phenomena without adding a supernatural designer or religious authority.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if natural processes provide sufficient explanatory paths, present scientific unknowns do not license supernatural conclusions, and specifically Christian claims lack necessary evidential support.

motionBridge.description: Show that the phenomena named in the motion can be approached through naturalistic explanation without requiring Christian theism.

centralBridges.description: Explain how apparent design, biological complexity, information, and regularities can arise or persist through unguided natural processes.
Justify withholding supernatural conclusions while testable scientific explanations remain open or under development.
Provide an account of moral conduct and reflection based on evolved social dispositions and consideration of consequences.
Require objective support for religious claims beyond their historical influence, psychological comfort, or inherited authority.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Apply methodological economy by adding a divine cause only if natural explanation proves insufficient in principle.
Treat natural laws as human descriptions of observed regularities rather than commands that necessarily imply a lawgiver.

sectionSelections.title: Design, mechanism, and explanatory method
sectionSelections.rationale: This issue establishes whether scientific mechanisms displace a designer, remain compatible with divine agency, or should be pursued without adding a supernatural explanation.

proSelections.proposition: Scientific mechanisms do not exclude a personal creator who originated and designed those mechanisms.
The universe's mathematical intelligibility and humanity's ability to do science are better accounted for by theism than atheism.

conSelections.proposition: Scientific progress can explain apparent design in organisms, physical laws, and the universe without requiring a designer.
Inquiry should pursue complete natural explanations under minimal assumptions and add God only if divine agency proves indispensable.

sectionSelections.title: Life's origin, evolution, and biological information
sectionSelections.rationale: The origin of replication and the status of DNA information determine whether evolutionary and chemical processes suffice or whether biological organization points to intelligence.

proSelections.proposition: Evolution presupposes a replicator and therefore does not explain life's origin, while DNA's semiotic character supports an inference to mind.
Natural processes can transmit biological information, but their production of symbolic information has not been shown, making intelligence relevant to its origin.

conSelections.proposition: Natural selection can accumulate biological complexity from chemical beginnings without requiring an intelligent cause.
Biological information can exist, be transmitted, modified, and interpreted through evolution without having been caused by intelligence.

sectionSelections.title: Cosmic origin, laws, and life-permitting conditions
sectionSelections.rationale: This issue bears on whether mathematical structure, existence, natural regularities, and life-permitting conditions require creative intelligence or admit a naturalistic ultimate account.

proSelections.proposition: The null set is not absolute nothingness, and mathematical descriptions lack causal power, leaving a creative mind as an explanation of cosmic intelligibility.
The extreme fine-tuning of cosmic conditions and constants for carbon-based life is evidence relevant to an inference of design.

conSelections.proposition: A fundamentally mathematical reality may emerge from nothing without external intelligent intervention, by analogy with mathematical construction from the null set.
Natural laws are human summaries of regularities that can emerge from entities' uncontrolled physical behavior without a divine lawgiver.

sectionSelections.title: Morality, responsibility, and ultimate hope
sectionSelections.rationale: The competing accounts must explain moral judgment and responsibility, while claims about death and ultimate justice test what each worldview permits beyond present biological life.

proSelections.proposition: Atheistic naturalism cannot consistently sustain moral responsibility if reality contains no objective good or evil and behavior is only DNA's working.
Atheists can behave morally, but atheism itself lacks a rational foundation for morality and ultimate justice.

conSelections.proposition: Morality can rest on evolved social dispositions and reflective assessment of actions and their consequences rather than divine authority.
Mental and spiritual experience depends on physiological brain processes, leaving belief in an afterlife unsupported wishful thinking.

sectionSelections.title: Historical and experiential grounds for Christian belief
sectionSelections.rationale: General arguments for intelligence do not alone establish Christianity, so the route requires assessment of historical and experiential evidence against naturalistic objections to religious authority and conditioning.

proSelections.proposition: The rise of Christianity and the empty tomb are historical facts requiring explanation and support serious consideration of the resurrection.
Nature can indicate a creator's existence and power, but full Christian theism requires additional historical, biblical, experiential, and personal evidence.

conSelections.proposition: Religion is an inherited primitive explanatory framework, whereas collective inquiry using objective evidence can understand the cosmos without religious authority.
Religious belief may provide comfort, but imposing it on children constrains intellectual freedom and opportunities in their present lives.
